newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore, Waterford favour merger.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore, Waterford favour merger.

text.p: A proposed merger between Ireland's largest dairy companies Avonmore Foods Plc AVFa.L and Waterford Foods Plc got the thumbs up on Friday when shareholders for both groups voted overwhelmingly in favour of the merger.
Waterford Foods said 83 percent of those present at a special meeting voted yes to a merger with Avonmore. The meeting was held in the southern county of Waterford on Friday afternoon.
"This is indeed an historic day for farmers in the southeast. It augers well for the future of the dairy industry," Waterford Co-op chairman John Downey said in a statement.
Earlier 97.6 percent of Avonmore Creameries members, who own 63.9 percent of Avonmore Foods Plc, voted in favour of the merger, at a meeting held simultaneously in the midland town of Kilkenny.
Avonmore chairman John Duggan said the vote "represents the first important step towards the successful conclusion of the merger of Avonmore and Waterford."

To succeed the merger has to be approved by 75 percent of the farmers who attend two consecutive extraordinary general meetings. The second meeting is scheduled for July 25 to ratify Friday's outcome.
If approved, the merger will weld two of Ireland's premier food companies with a joint turnover of 2.5 billion Irish pounds ($3.8 billion) and pre-tax profits of 71.5 million.
This will create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.

Analysts said the merged company's milk production would far outstrip the dairy operations of Britain's Northern Foods Plc and Unigate Plc and its cheese production would account for 20 percent of the British market.
This is the second time in six years that Avonmore has attempted to merge with Waterford after a similar attempt in 1991 failed.

The two companies have interests in continental Europe, Britain and America. Avonmore has interests in meat products, animal foodstuffs and agricultural products including grain. It has processing operations in Ireland, Britain, Belgium and the United States, Japan, Korea and Singapore.
Waterford is engaged in dairy-based food products, fruit juices and animal foodstuffs and has processing plants in Ireland, Britain and America.
